# Lab Map {#sec-lab-map}

The companion lab is [forensics-docker-lab](https://forensics.borck.education/). It runs a Docker or Podman forensic workstation and supplies pre-acquired evidence for the Cloudcore case.

| Lab | Focus | Chapter | What it teaches | What it cannot teach |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Overview | Case, scope, environment limits | 1, 3 | Incident framing and analysis boundary | Physical seizure and live acquisition |
| Lab 1 | USB imaging and deleted files | 4 | File system triage, metadata recovery, carving, hashing | Write blocking a physical device |
| Lab 2 | Memory forensics | 5 | Volatility workflow, process tree, modules, connections | Capturing live RAM |
| Lab 3 | Email and logs | 6 | Mailbox parsing, headers, attachments, log correlation | Proving a recipient read a message |
| Lab 4 | Network analysis | 6 | Flow analysis, DNS, protocols, exfiltration indicators | Reading encrypted payloads |
| Lab 5 | Final report | 7, 8 | Timeline, correlation, findings, limitations | Legal judgment or disciplinary decision |

## Environment boundary

The lab is an analysis environment. It can analyse disk images, memory samples, mailboxes, logs and packet captures. It cannot write-block or image a physical device, capture live RAM, sniff a live network interface or seize hardware.

Read the lab's own scope statement before you begin:

- [Environment scope](https://github.com/michael-borck/forensics-docker-lab#-environment-scope-what-docker-can--cannot-do)
- [Evidence sources](https://github.com/michael-borck/forensics-docker-lab/blob/main/docs/evidence-sources.md)

## Suggested lab order

1. Read the case brief and write your questions.
2. Read the lab scenario and environment scope.
3. Complete Lab 1 and record the evidence.
4. Complete Lab 2 with a memory sample.
5. Complete Labs 3 and 4, then correlate.
6. Complete Lab 5 with your own timeline and report.
7. Review your report against the limitations in Chapter 8.
